title: Psychology takes toys seriously, with Barry Kudrowitz, PhD, and Doris Bergen, PhD

sentences.en: It's that time of year when parents and other caregivers race to find the hottest toys and stock up on classic favorites, from Poppets to Pokemon, from Squishmallows to Legos.
sentences.zh: 又到了每年这个时候，父母和其他看护人争先恐后地寻找最热门的玩具，囤积各种经典畅销品，从 Poppets 到宝可梦，从 Squishmallows 到乐高。

sentences.en: Toys might seem frivolous, but to psychologists, they're a subject for serious study.
sentences.zh: 玩具看起来可能微不足道，但对心理学家而言，它们是一个严肃的研究课题。

sentences.en: Researchers have long known that children learn best through play.
sentences.zh: 研究人员很早就知道，儿童通过游戏学得最好。

sentences.en: Play is how kids stretch their brains and develop crucial cognitive, social, and other skills.
sentences.zh: 游戏是孩子们开阔思维、培养关键认知、社交及其他技能的方式。

sentences.en: And toys are a fundamental part of playtime.
sentences.zh: 而玩具是游戏时间中不可或缺的基本组成部分。

sentences.en: But what makes something a good toy?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让一样东西成为好玩具？

sentences.en: Indeed, what makes something a toy at all?
sentences.zh: 事实上，又是什么让一样东西配得上“玩具”二字？

sentences.en: Why do some toys stand the test of time, while others are just a one-season wonder?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些玩具经受住了时间的考验，而另一些只是一季即逝的奇迹？

sentences.en: What's the difference between fun and educational toys?
sentences.zh: 好玩有趣的玩具和益智玩具之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Why do we assign gender appropriateness to some toys and not to others?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们给某些玩具赋予性别属性，而其他玩具则没有？

sentences.en: How do kids' toy preferences change as they age, and how has technology changed what toys are, and the way kids play with toys?
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，孩子们对玩具的偏好是如何变化的？科技又是如何改变玩具本身的形态以及孩子们玩玩具的方式的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: Our first is Dr. Barry Kudrowitz, an associate professor and director of product design at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, where he teaches classes in toy product design.
sentences.zh: 第一位是巴里·库德罗维茨博士，他是明尼苏达大学双城分校产品设计的副教授兼主任，在那里他教授玩具产品设计课程。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz has a PhD in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where he studied creativity, humor, and idea generation.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士拥有麻省理工学院机械工程博士学位，他在那里研究了创造力、幽默感和创意生成。

sentences.en: And he has studied how play can fuel creativity and innovation.
sentences.zh: 并且他研究了游戏如何能激发创造力和创新。

sentences.en: In addition to his academic career, he's also a toy designer.
sentences.zh: 除了学术生涯，他本身也是一名玩具设计师。

sentences.en: Highlights of his work include the Ketchup Crapper, an anthropomorphic roller skating ketchup
sentences.zh: 他标志性的作品包括番茄酱便盆椅（Ketchup Crapper），这是一个拟人化的旱冰鞋番茄酱

sentences.en: bottle that he designed as a grad student, and the Nerf Atom Blaster, a Nerf toy sold by Hasbro more than five years.
sentences.zh: 瓶，是他在读研究生时设计的；还有一个是 Nerf Atom Blaster，这是一款由孩之宝销售了五年多的 Nerf 玩具。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Dr. Doris Bergen, a distinguished professor emerita of educational psychology at Miami University in Oxford, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是多丽丝·伯根博士，她是俄亥俄州牛津迈阿密大学教育心理学的杰出荣休教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Bergen began her career as a pre-kindergarten and elementary school teacher.
sentences.zh: 伯根博士的职业生涯始于学前班和小学老师。

sentences.en: And over her long academic career, she has explored the many ways that play is crucial to children's development.
sentences.zh: 在她漫长的学术生涯中，她探讨了游戏对儿童发展至关重要的诸多方面。

sentences.en: She has studied play and humor in early and middle childhood, the effects of technology-enhanced toys, and cross-cultural considerations in play, among many other topics.
sentences.zh: 她研究过幼儿和中童期的游戏与幽默、科技赋能玩具的影响、游戏中的跨文化考量等众多课题。

sentences.en: Dr. Bergen has authored or edited more than a dozen books, including her most recent,
sentences.zh: 伯根博士撰写或主编了十多本书，其中包括她最近的一本著作：

sentences.en: The Handbook of Developmentally Appropriate Toys, which was published in March 2021.
sentences.zh: 《发展适宜性玩具手册》，该书于 2021 年 3 月出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So let's start with a broad question, which we usually do.
sentences.zh: 那我们先从一个宏观的问题开始，我们通常都这样做。

sentences.en: What is the purpose of toys, and what makes something a good toy or makes something a toy at all?
sentences.zh: 玩具的目的是什么？究竟是什么让一样东西成为好玩具，或者说是什么让一样东西配得上被称为玩具？

sentences.en: For example, can a stick or a rock be a toy?
sentences.zh: 例如，一根树枝或一块石头能成为玩具吗？

sentences.en: Actually, toys have existed for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，玩具已经存在了很久很久。

sentences.en: You can even find them in early sites.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在早期的遗址中找到它们。

sentences.en: And so some of the typical toys that children still play with today, like dolls and wheel toys, things of that sort, have been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们今天仍在玩的一些典型玩具，比如洋娃娃和带轮子的玩具之类，已经存在了很长时间。

sentences.en: But I would say that the purpose of toys, in my view, is to enhance children's play, because children will play even if there aren't any toys.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，在我看来，玩具的目的是为了增强儿童的游戏，因为即使没有任何玩具，孩子们也会玩耍。

sentences.en: They'll find sticks, or they'll find rocks, or they'll find other things to use in their pretend play and in their game play.
sentences.zh: 他们会寻找树枝、石头或其他东西，用在他们的假装游戏和游玩当中。

sentences.en: But toys are a means of enhancing the play and making it more creative and often more elaborative.
sentences.zh: 但玩具是一种增强游戏、让游戏更具创意且通常更丰富多彩的手段。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: Toys are a tool for play.
sentences.zh: 玩具就是游戏的工具。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a difference between a toy and a toy product.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，玩具和玩具产品之间是有区别的。

sentences.en: There are certain toys that are designed by people to be intended to be used for play.
sentences.zh: 有些玩具是人们专门设计用来玩耍的。

sentences.en: And then there's things that are not designed, you know, intended to be used for play that children still play with, like cardboard boxes and spoons and rakes and stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 还有一些东西并非本意被设计用于玩耍，但孩子们依然拿它们当玩具玩，比如纸箱、勺子、耙子之类，对吧？

sentences.en: There's still toys, but maybe they're not toy products.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然是玩具，但也许它们不是玩具产品。

sentences.en: And many toy products are designed by people who have ideas about what they think is good for children to play with.
sentences.zh: 许多玩具产品的设计者都有一些想法，关于他们认为什么对孩子们玩耍有益。

sentences.en: Maybe they think they'll learn particular things from them.
sentences.zh: 也许他们认为孩子们能从中学会某些特定的东西。

sentences.en: They have different expectations about the toys.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些玩具有着不同的期望。

sentences.en: And I would say a really good toy is one that doesn't do everything itself, but has the child do it.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，一个真正的好玩具是那种不会包办一切、而是让孩子自己去动手的玩具。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, I think some toys designed do too much, and there isn't really even room for children to do very much with them.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我认为一些设计出来的玩具做的事情太多了，甚至没有给孩子们留下多少发挥的空间。

sentences.en: And so those toys typically don't have very lasting value.
sentences.zh: 因此，这类玩具通常没有太持久的价值。

sentences.en: Maybe kids will play with them for a while, learn what they do,
sentences.zh: 也许孩子们会玩上一会儿，了解它们的功能，

sentences.en: and then they'll probably turn them into something else and use them in a different way or maybe discard them altogether.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可能会把它们变成别的东西，以不同的方式使用，或者干脆将其丢弃。

sentences.en: And are those things that you think about, Dr. Kudrowitz, when you're designing toys or teaching people how to design toys?
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，你在设计玩具或教别人如何设计玩具时，会考虑这些事情吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking about them, but not necessarily the students.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会考虑，但不一定要求学生考虑。

sentences.en: And even when we do playtesting, it's not necessarily even the children that we playtest are thinking about those things.
sentences.zh: 甚至当我们在进行游戏测试时，参与测试的儿童也未必会去考虑这些事情。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, it's what is trendy or popular that they might gravitate to.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，他们可能会被时髦或流行的东西所吸引。

sentences.en: But I also think that what makes a toy a good toy is that it can be used in a variety of different contexts, and it doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，让一个玩具成为好玩具的原因在于，它可以在各种不同的语境下使用，而且它不会“过时”。

sentences.en: You know, you can use it for generations, for example, or in multiple different ways of playing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如你可以世世代代地使用它，或者用多种不同的方式去玩。

sentences.en: You know, like the cardboard box is a great example.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像纸箱就是一个极好的例子。

sentences.en: We actually have a box in our dining room right now from a couch, but it's been played with by the children for months now.
sentences.zh: 我们餐现在就放着一个从沙发包装里拆出来的纸箱，但孩子们已经玩了好几个月了。

sentences.en: And we left this giant box in the dining room, and they play with that more than, you know, all the toys we've gotten so far.
sentences.zh: 我们把这个巨大的纸箱留在餐厅里，他们玩这个纸箱的时间比我们买给他们的所有玩具加起来还要多。

sentences.en: It's a fort.
sentences.zh: 它是一座堡垒。

sentences.en: It's a rocket ship.
sentences.zh: 它是一艘火箭飞船。

sentences.en: They're drawing all over the walls.
sentences.zh: 他们在墙壁上画得到处都是。

sentences.en: They're cutting out holes.
sentences.zh: 他们在上面戳洞。

sentences.en: And that was free.
sentences.zh: 而且那是免费的。

sentences.en: And it's compostable.
sentences.zh: 它还是可堆肥的。

sentences.en: And I think it's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: There are sort of different kinds of play, you know, of course, and different kind of toys facilitate different kinds.
sentences.zh: 当然，游戏有各种不同的种类，不同种类的玩具也能促进不同种类的游戏。

sentences.en: If you're thinking of just kind of exploratory play or manipulative play, that's one kind of toy that will work for that.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑的只是探索性游戏或操作性游戏，那么某种特定的玩具就能派上用场。

sentences.en: If you're looking at pretend play, there's a whole range of other kinds of toys that are really facilitative of pretense.
sentences.zh: 如果你关注的是假装游戏，还有一大类其他玩具非常有助于促进假装行为。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's game play of all different kinds and very different kinds of toys for that.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有各种各样不同的游戏，也有截然不同的玩具适用于这些游戏。

sentences.en: And there's certainly some overlap among those.
sentences.zh: 这些玩具之间肯定有一些重叠。

sentences.en: But the type of play that the child is going to do, if it's active play, quiet play, or of various sorts, will usually need, or at least there'll be an expectation,
sentences.zh: 但是孩子将要进行的游玩类型，无论是积极好动的游戏、安静的游戏，还是其他各种游戏，通常都需要，或者至少会有一种期望，

sentences.en: that different kinds of toys will meet the needs for different kinds of play.
sentences.zh: 即不同种类的玩具能够满足不同种类游戏的需求。

sentences.en: So, a lot of parents think that toys come in basically two categories.
sentences.zh: 所以，很多父母认为玩具基本上分为两大类。

sentences.en: And, Dr. Bergen, you just described several categories, not just two.
sentences.zh: 伯根博士，你刚才描述了好几个类别，而不仅仅是两类。

sentences.en: But for parents, they think they're educational toys, like those that are designed to teach science or math or reading.
sentences.zh: 但对于父母来说，他们认为有益智玩具，比如那些旨在教授科学、数学或阅读的玩具。

sentences.en: And then there are toys that are for fun, which covers pretty much everything else.
sentences.zh: 然后还有纯粹供娱乐的玩具，几乎涵盖了其他所有玩具。

sentences.en: Is that a valid distinction?
sentences.zh: 这种区分成立吗？

sentences.en: And is there a difference between a fun toy and an educational toy?
sentences.zh: 好玩的玩具和益智玩具之间有区别吗？

sentences.en: Should there be?
sentences.zh: 本该如此吗？

sentences.en: I mean, going back to the very first thing we talked about, the primary purpose of a toy is play.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回到我们讨论的第一件事，玩具的主要目的是游戏。

sentences.en: And if the primary purpose is to teach something, it may not be a very good toy.
sentences.zh: 如果它的主要目的是教学，那它可能就不是一个好玩具。

sentences.en: But, you know, that being said, play is how we learn.
sentences.zh: 但是，话虽如此，游戏正是我们学习的方式。

sentences.en: That's how we've learned skills growing up.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在成长过程中学习技能的方式。

sentences.en: We learned developmental skills, cognitive skills, physical skills.
sentences.zh: 我们学习发展技能、认知技能、身体技能。

sentences.en: And so, you could also argue that no matter what kind of play, if you're engaging in play, you could argue that you're learning something.
sentences.zh: 因此，你也可以认为，无论进行何种游戏，只要你投入其中，就可以认为你正在学到东西。

sentences.en: And so, it's a little bit hard to separate those two.
sentences.zh: 所以，要将这两者严格区分开来有点困难。

sentences.en: But I don't necessarily like the idea of a toy being primarily designed to be teaching you something.
sentences.zh: 但我并不太喜欢把玩具主要设计成用来教你某种东西这种想法。

sentences.en: I would agree.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞同。

sentences.en: I think that's maybe more of a marketing distinction than it is a toy distinction.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与其说是玩具上的分类，不如说是营销上的区分。

sentences.en: Because I think children learn from every type of play and from every type of toy.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为孩子们从每一种游戏和每一种玩具中都能学到东西。

sentences.en: They may not be learning a specific thing like letters or, you know, whatever the toy maker thought they would do.
sentences.zh: 他们可能没有学到具体的某样东西，比如字母，或者玩具制造商原以为他们会学会的东西。

sentences.en: But they also learn many other social and physical and intellectual skills from just about any toy.
sentences.zh: 但他们也通过几乎任何玩具学到了许多其他的社交、身体和智力技能。

sentences.en: So, I think the distinction educational toys is primarily a distinction for parents and for teachers and people who think that, oh, if it says educational,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为“益智玩具”这个分类主要是针对父母、老师以及那些认为“哦，如果上面写着益智，

sentences.en: it's going to have a greater educational factor.
sentences.zh: 它就会有更高教育价值”的人而设立的。

sentences.en: The other way that educational toy could be seen is if there's a specific kind of teaching that the adult wants a child to have.
sentences.zh: 看待益智玩具的另一种方式是，如果成年人希望孩子掌握某种特定的教学内容。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, sometimes those kind of toys that are very specifically designed to teach a certain thing are either not used very often by the child,
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，有时那些专门为教授某项特定内容而设计的玩具，要么不常被孩子使用，

sentences.en: or the child transforms them in some way into pretend or something else.
sentences.zh: 要么被孩子以某种方式转化成了假装游戏或其他用途。

sentences.en: And they don't exactly use them in the same way that the person who designed them thought they would use them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们使用的方式并不完全符合设计者预期的那样。

sentences.en: And I think that's an amazing thing that kids can do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是孩子们能够做到的了不起的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I've known parents, for example, who've decided that they never want their children to have a toy gun.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认识一些父母，比如他们决定永远不让自己的孩子拥有玩具枪。

sentences.en: And somehow, kids will figure out how to make something into a gun.
sentences.zh: 但不知怎么的，孩子们总能想出办法把某种东西变成一把枪。

sentences.en: If they want to play with guns, they're going to have a make-believe gun, right?
sentences.zh: 如果他们想玩打仗游戏，他们就会弄一把假想的枪，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just the creative end of childhood.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是童年创造力的体现。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz, you were quoted in a recent article talking about the fact that toy makers worry that kids are losing interest in toys at a younger age than they used to.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，最近有一篇文章引用了你的话，谈到玩具制造商担心孩子们对玩具失去兴趣的年龄比以往更小了。

sentences.en: Is that actually happening?
sentences.zh: 这种现象真的在发生吗？

sentences.en: And if it is, why do you think so?
sentences.zh: 如果确实如此，你认为是什么原因造成的？

sentences.en: So this is related to the concept of age compression.
sentences.zh: 这与“年龄压缩”的概念有关。

sentences.en: There's probably other terms related to this.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他与此相关的术语。

sentences.en: We talked to Doris about that, but it seems like kids are playing with the stuff that the older kids were playing with in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们和多丽丝讨论过这一点，但看起来现在的孩子正在玩过去大龄儿童才玩的东西。

sentences.en: And this may be more of an artifact of technology advancing to the degree that things that we used to play with in the past were,
sentences.zh: 这可能更多是科技发展到一定程度带来的产物，因为过去我们玩的东西，

sentences.en: I don't want to say dumb, but they didn't have high tech inside because that was expensive.
sentences.zh: 我不是想说它们“蠢”，而是它们的内在没有高科技，因为那时高科技很昂贵。

sentences.en: And in today's society, you can put LEDs in anything, and it's relatively low coSt.
sentences.zh: 而在当今社会，你可以在任何东西里装上 LED 灯，而且成本相对较低。

sentences.en: You could put motors in things and processors, and there's computers in everything in my pocket right now.
sentences.zh: 你可以在物品中放入马达和处理器，现在我口袋里的每样东西里都有电脑。

sentences.en: And it's not that much more expensive in today's society.
sentences.zh: 在当今社会，这并没有贵出多少。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the things that children are playing with today are not necessarily video games, but they're more like technology.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们今天玩的很多东西不一定是电子游戏，但它们更类似于科技产品。

sentences.en: And in the market space, some of those things kind of get lumped into consumer electronics and not necessarily in the toy aisle.
sentences.zh: 在市场上，其中一些东西被归入了消费电子产品类，而不一定在玩具过道里。

sentences.en: And so, again, it kind of goes back to maybe marketing in some ways, but also you're not necessarily seeing kids play with the same toys as they were years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，这在某种程度上又回到了营销问题，但你也确实不再看到孩子们像多年前那样玩同样的玩具了。

sentences.en: And there's a lot more screens and digital things in their hands.
sentences.zh: 而且他们手里有更多的屏幕和数字产品。

sentences.en: As a longtime observer of play and interviewing of adults' memories of their childhood play,
sentences.zh: 作为一名长期的游戏观察者以及成年人童年游戏记忆的采访者，

sentences.en: I definitely agree with Barry that the way play, the time and the experiences children have in play now has changed quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我绝对赞同巴里的看法，即现在孩子们在游戏中的方式、时间和体验已经发生了相当大的变化。

sentences.en: But when you think back to your own play time, or certainly many other people who I've interviewed,
sentences.zh: 但当你回想自己的游戏时间，或者肯定我采访过的许多其他人时，

sentences.en: they recall long periods of time where they pretty much could decide what they wanted to do with the time.
sentences.zh: 他们会回忆起很长一段时间里，他们几乎可以自己决定如何利用这些时间。

sentences.en: And the kind of play materials they had were ones that they created.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有的游戏材料都是他们自己创造的。

sentences.en: They made the toy talk, or they made the toy walk, or they did whatever it was with their own imagination.
sentences.zh: 他们让玩具说话，让玩具走路，或者用他们自己的想象力做任何事情。

sentences.en: And now, so many of the toys, the toy does everything.
sentences.zh: 而现在，太多的玩具把所有事情都包办了。

sentences.en: There's really not much for the child to do.
sentences.zh: 留给孩子做的事情真的不多了。

sentences.en: And so, that toy is not going to be nearly as important in terms of children's development or their interest level.
sentences.zh: 因此，就儿童的发展或他们的兴趣水平而言，这种玩具不会那么重要。

sentences.en: Because if you're just, there's 10 buttons to push, and you've pushed all 10 buttons, and then that's really the end of what you can do with the toy.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是按了 10 个按钮，然后把这 10 个按钮都按完了，那基本上就是你能用这个玩具做的全部事情了。

sentences.en: Usually, what you see the child do is either put it away and not look at it anymore, or pick it up and pretend it's something altogether different,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你会看到孩子要么把它收起来不再看它，要么把它拿起来假装它是完全不同的东西，

sentences.en: and use imagination and do something else with it.
sentences.zh: 发挥想象力用它做点别的。

sentences.en: So, I do think that that change, and certainly that idea that experiences have gone down to lower levels,
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实认为这种变化，以及体验水平下降的这种观点，

sentences.en: is not just related to toys, but it's pervasive across a lot of other things for children today.
sentences.zh: 不仅与玩具有关，而且在当今儿童的许多其他事物中也是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: But I do think, I've often thought the people designing the technology are the ones that are having the playful time.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，我经常觉得设计科技产品的人才是真正玩得开心的人。

sentences.en: Because they're the ones that get to figure out what to do with it, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为他们才是弄清楚如何使用它的人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, it's the grown-ups who are coming up with these ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以，是成年人在想出这些点子。

sentences.en: The kids aren't asking for the toys to be, yeah.
sentences.zh: 并不是孩子们要求玩具变成那样的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, are you recommending that parents give their kids, like, dolls that don't do anything except sit there?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是在建议父母给孩子买那种除了坐在那里什么都不做的洋娃娃吗？

sentences.en: They still make those.
sentences.zh: 现在还在生产这种玩具。

sentences.en: I know!
sentences.zh: 我知道！

sentences.en: One of the things that concerns me a great deal is, if you remember back to your childhood,
sentences.zh: 让我非常担忧的事情之一是，如果你回想起自己的童年，

sentences.en: maybe all summer you didn't have anything to do except just figure out what to play with yourself.
sentences.zh: 也许整个夏天你除了自己琢磨着玩什么之外，没有任何事可做。

sentences.en: Now, children's lives are very structured, both after school and in summer.
sentences.zh: 现在，孩子们的生活安排得非常紧凑，无论是放学后还是暑假期间。

sentences.en: And so, they don't necessarily have those long periods of time where they can really create their own play world.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们不一定有那种长长的时间段来真正创造他们自己的游戏世界。

sentences.en: So, that's a very, very different thing that we see now.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们现在看到的非常、非常不同的情况。

sentences.en: So, let me ask a kind of a developmental question.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我问一个关于发展的问题。

sentences.en: Maybe this is for Dr. Bergen, although you're both welcome to answer it.
sentences.zh: 也许这个问题是问伯根博士的，不过你们两位都可以回答。

sentences.en: But what happens to children who grow up without actual toys?
sentences.zh: 但是，那些在成长过程中没有真正玩具的孩子们会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Do they develop differently, and are they different as adults?
sentences.zh: 他们的发育会有所不同吗？成年后他们会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: I really don't know of any research that's really looked at children who grow up without play.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，确实没有什么研究真正关注过在没有玩具的环境中长大的孩子。

sentences.en: Because the research that, let's say, would be done in a country where there were very few toys, show that children play anyway.
sentences.zh: 因为假设在某个几乎没有什么玩具的国家进行的研究表明，孩子们无论如何都会玩。

sentences.en: They don't necessarily have to have toys to play.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定非得有玩具才能玩。

sentences.en: So, it's more of a question, I guess, if you had children who had to go to work at age six or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想这更像是一个假设问题：比如那些六岁就得去工作或者类似情况的孩子。

sentences.en: And I don't really know.
sentences.zh: 而且我其实并不知道。

sentences.en: That's a very important issue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: It probably should be studied.
sentences.zh: 它或许应该被纳入研究。

sentences.en: But I don't really know if it's the case that there are children who haven't any play experiences.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定是否真的存在完全没有任何游戏体验的孩子。

sentences.en: But they may be very different kinds of play experiences.
sentences.zh: 不过他们可能会有完全不同种类的游戏体验。

sentences.en: They may have play experiences where they use whatever is in their environment and create their own play,
sentences.zh: 他们的游戏体验可能是利用环境中的任何东西来创造自己的游戏，

sentences.en: as compared to the kind of play that Barry was mentioning, where they have many, many toys,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，正如巴里刚才提到那种他们拥有许许多多玩具的游戏，

sentences.en: but a lot of toys have all these characteristics that just require you to push a button or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但很多玩具都有这样的特点：只需要你按个按钮或者做类似的事情。

sentences.en: So, I think there's a wide range of play experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为游戏体验的范围非常广泛。

sentences.en: But at least in my experience, children, even if they have 10 or 15 minutes of their own time, are going to find something to play.
sentences.zh: 但至少在我的经验中，孩子们即使只有10到15分钟的空闲时间，也会找点东西来玩。

sentences.en: Going back to the last thing that Dora said, on technology, maybe restricting play.
sentences.zh: 回到多拉刚才说的最后一件事，关于技术可能在限制游戏。

sentences.en: And that is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That happens.
sentences.zh: 这种情况是存在的。

sentences.en: But it can also be used for good.
sentences.zh: 但它也可以被用于积极的方面。

sentences.en: And designers can create open-ended play experiences for children, taking advantage of technology.
sentences.zh: 设计师可以利用技术为孩子们创造开放式的游戏体验。

sentences.en: So, you know, they could create new types of musical instruments or things where children can program their own things to do whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们可以创造新型的乐器，或者让孩子们自己编写程序来实现任何想要的效果。

sentences.en: What is the Spider-Man quote?
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛侠的那句名言是什么来着？

sentences.en: You know, with great power comes great responsibility.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，能力越大，责任越大。

sentences.en: You know, it's in the hands of the designer to create those good toys.
sentences.zh: 你知道，设计出好的玩具掌握在设计师的手中。

sentences.en: I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: I just think that if there's only one way to use a toy, that it's hard for children to use it for a long time period.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，如果一种玩具只有一种玩法，孩子们就很难长时间使用它。

sentences.en: So, as long as, you know, there are many different things to do with it, even if it's got a lot of technology enhancement, I think it can be a toy that has a lot of playability.
sentences.zh: 所以，只要它能有许多不同的玩法，即使它带有很多科技升级，我认为它也能成为一个具有极高可玩性的玩具。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Kudrow, it's one for you.
sentences.zh: 那么，库德罗博士，这个问题是给你的。

sentences.en: Do commercial toy designers think about developmental psychology while they're designing toys?
sentences.zh: 商业玩具设计师在设计玩具时会考虑发展心理学吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do toy companies routinely have psychologists that they consult with, that they have them on staff?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，玩具公司通常会咨询心理学家，或者在员工中配备心理学家吗？

sentences.en: And are those toys different or better?
sentences.zh: 这些玩具会有所不同或者更好吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think this is probably a question for Doris, because I think she's consulted for those big companies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这个问题大概应该问多丽丝，因为我觉得她曾为那些大公司担任过顾问。

sentences.en: But I can say that, you know, not all toy companies are large and can afford consultation.
sentences.zh: 不过我可以这么说，并不是所有的玩具公司都是大公司，都有能力负担咨询费用。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's probably generally the big players that could bring in consultants like Doris on these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，通常也就是那些大公司才能在这方面请来像多丽丝这样的顾问。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll pick up on that, because I did, and a lot of other developmental psychology people, did do a lot of work for Fisher Price.
sentences.zh: 是的，我接着这个话题说，因为我确实做过，许多其他发展心理学界的人也为费雪公司做过大量工作。

sentences.en: They had their headquarters in New York for a long time, and they would bring us there, and we would look at the toys at the stage before they were in their final stage.
sentences.zh: 他们很长一段时间在纽约设有总部，他们会把我们请到那里，在玩具最终定型之前的阶段让我们去查看它们。

sentences.en: And we would evaluate them and, you know, describe what we thought might be good developmental aspects and what would work and what wouldn't and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们会对它们进行评估，并描述我们认为哪些是好的发展特性、什么行得通、什么行不通等等。

sentences.en: And that was really a very important thing, and that's why Fisher Price toys were always so very playable and very good for development.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一件非常重要的事情，这就是为什么费雪的玩具总是那么好玩，而且对儿童发育非常有益。

sentences.en: Once Fisher Price got taken over, I think, by another company, I don't think they still have those consultants that they did at that time.
sentences.zh: 一旦费雪被另一家公司收购，我想他们大概就不再像以前那样聘请这些顾问了。

sentences.en: But there may be some other toy companies that do have consultants, but I always thought that was really a good process,
sentences.zh: 不过可能还有其他一些玩具公司确实有顾问，但我一直认为这是一个非常好的流程，

sentences.en: because it was at the time of where there could still be some fine-tuning of the toy, but the basic toy was already designed.
sentences.zh: 因为它正处于还能对玩具进行微调的阶段，尽管基础玩具已经设计好了。

sentences.en: And I think that made the toys really more playable and more developmentally appropriate by having that input from psychologists.
sentences.zh: 我认为通过引入心理学家的意见，真的让这些玩具变得更有可玩性，也更符合儿童的发展阶段。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Bergen, you studied play in China.
sentences.zh: 那么，伯根博士，你曾在中国研究过游戏。

sentences.en: Dr. Kudrowitz, you worked on toy design in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 库德罗维茨博士，你曾在荷兰从事过玩具设计。

sentences.en: Do the types of toys that kids like to play with vary much around the world, or are they pretty much universal?
sentences.zh: 世界各地的小朋友喜欢玩的玩具类型差异很大，还是基本上是通用的？

sentences.en: I guess I would say, as far as China, I didn't see any big differences.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说，就中国而言，我没有看到什么巨大的差异。

sentences.en: When I was there, there wasn't a lot of...
sentences.zh: 我在那里的时候，并没有太多……

sentences.en: Where I was, it was not a rich environment, and so a lot of the play was pretty basic.
sentences.zh: 我待的地方并不是一个富裕的环境，所以很多游戏都非常基础。

sentences.en: But, you know, things like balls and dolls and toy trucks and various things like that were pretty much the same there.
sentences.zh: 但是，像球、洋娃娃、玩具卡车以及各种类似的东西，在那里基本上都是一样的。

sentences.en: They also played a lot of games outdoors, and outdoor play was very big at the time I was in China.
sentences.zh: 他们也玩很多户外游戏，在我待在中国的时候，户外游戏非常盛行。

sentences.en: I really don't know what it's like now, but that was quite a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道现在是什么样了，但那是相当久以前的事了。

sentences.en: What about in the Netherlands?
sentences.zh: 荷兰的情况呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't too different.
sentences.zh: 也没有太大的不同。

sentences.en: I'm always looking for new stuff, and so being in a new environment, I felt inspired, and I felt like all the toys were cooler there, because they're all, you know, different.
sentences.zh: 我一直在寻找新奇的东西，所以身处一个新的环境让我感到很受启发，我觉得那里的所有玩具都更酷，因为它们全都是与众不同的。

sentences.en: But I was just on sabbatical, actually, a couple years ago there, and it was my first introduction to Montessori.
sentences.zh: 但其实几年前我在那里做学术休假时，才是我第一次接触蒙台梭利教育。

sentences.en: And so we had our two-year-old in a Montessori daycare, and that style of play was really exciting.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将我们两岁的孩子送进了一家蒙台梭利日托中心，那种游戏方式真的让人非常兴奋。

sentences.en: The toys are like real stuff.
sentences.zh: 这里的玩具就像是真正的东西。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, prepping vegetables, you know, and cleaning and stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如准备蔬菜、搞卫生之类的。

sentences.en: And it's turning these everyday activities, you know, into play in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它们把这些日常活动转化成了游戏。

sentences.en: They have these kinder borderei, which are these kinder children farms, I guess, in the city.
sentences.zh: 他们有那种儿童农场，我想大概就是城里的那种儿童农场吧。

sentences.en: And you bring, you know, the family goes, and the kids take care of the animals, and they harvest vegetables, and they can go,
sentences.zh: 然后全家人一起去，孩子们照顾动物，收割蔬菜，他们可以去……

sentences.en: and they take these little tiny kid-sized wheelbarrows and shovels, and they go into the pasture, and they pick up cow poop.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着这种超小的儿童版独轮手推车和铲子，走到牧场里去捡牛粪。

sentences.en: And they do that for like an hour, and it's like, and it's play.
sentences.zh: 他们能干上整整一个小时，这就成了游戏。

sentences.en: This sounds like a con.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是个骗局。

sentences.en: This is how you make children do work.
sentences.zh: 这就是你们诱使儿童干活的方式。

sentences.en: No, and my son is like, can we go back to the farm and do more of that, right?
sentences.zh: 不，我的儿子会说：我们能回农场再玩一会儿那个吗？对吧？

sentences.en: And it's getting out into nature, connecting with animals.
sentences.zh: 这就是走到大自然中去，与动物建立连接。

sentences.en: You know, these are tools that aren't usually their size.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些通常都不是他们尺寸的工具。

sentences.en: And so there's some novelty about that, too.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中也有一些新鲜感。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 对的，

sentences.en: and I think that European play researchers have studied a lot of outdoor play because they're very much more focused on the natural environment and doing things outdoors in many of the countries in Europe,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为欧洲的游戏研究人员对户外游戏进行了大量研究，因为在欧洲的许多国家，他们更加关注自然环境以及在户外开展活动，

sentences.en: not so much here as they do there.
sentences.zh: 不像我们这里那样不如他们普遍。

sentences.en: But that's been a very strong emphasis, I think, in Europe altogether.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这一直是欧洲整体上非常强调的一个重点。

sentences.en: I think, though, that what I've found is that children's types of play are very similar wherever you are.
sentences.zh: 不过，我发现无论你在哪里，孩子们的游戏类型都非常相似。

sentences.en: And it may be that they use a manufactured toy that is designed specifically for something,
sentences.zh: 也许他们使用的是专门为某种目的而设计的量产玩具，

sentences.en: or if they're in an environment where there isn't a manufactured toy that fits whatever it is they want to do, they can invent something else to use.
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们身处一个没有现成量产玩具能满足他们需求的环境中，他们可以发明出别的东西来使用。

sentences.en: You can use a piece of toys, you can use a piece of wood to be a truck if you want to, if you don't have a real truck.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有真正的卡车，你可以用一块木头来当卡车。

sentences.en: You can use a rag and a ball to be a baby if you really don't have a real doll.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的没有真正的洋娃娃，你可以用一块抹布和一个球来当婴儿。

sentences.en: So I don't think that necessarily the types of things children play are that different.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为孩子们玩的东西类型会有那么大的差异。

sentences.en: I do think that there are many different materials they use in different places.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为他们在不同的地方使用了许多不同的材料。

sentences.en: But pretend play and game play and exploratory practice play, just doing over and over and expanding things,
sentences.zh: 但假装游戏、规则游戏和探索性练习游戏，就是那种一遍又一遍地重复和扩展事物的游戏，

sentences.en: those are all very common types of play that you would see just really wherever you were in the world, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是非常常见的游戏类型，无论你身处世界的哪个角落都能看到。

sentences.en: So I mentioned in the intro that Dr. Kudrowitz, one of your first toy designs was a pooping ketchup bottle.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到过，库德罗维茨博士，你的第一款玩具设计之一是一个会拉便便的番茄酱瓶。

sentences.en: And Dr. Bergen, you've been quoted in a couple of recent articles about why kids are so interested in potty humor and toys that defecate.
sentences.zh: 而伯根博士，最近的一些文章引用了你的话，探讨为什么小孩子对厕所幽默和会排泄的玩具这么感兴趣。

sentences.en: And since we're on the poop topic here, what is it about bathroom humor and potty-related toys that kids find so irresistible?
sentences.zh: 既然我们今天聊到了便便这个话题，为什么下流幽默和与便便相关的玩具对小孩子有着如此难以抗拒的吸引力呢？

sentences.en: Well, why do adults laugh at jokes that have those same kind of elements?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么成年人也会对包含同样元素的笑话发笑呢？

sentences.en: The only difference is that young children don't have a lot of experiences.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别在于，小孩子没有太多的阅历。

sentences.en: So bathroom stuff is one of the few, quote, shocking things that you're not supposed to talk about.
sentences.zh: 所以厕所相关的东西是少数几个所谓的、不应该拿来谈论的“令人震惊”的事情之一。

sentences.en: So obviously, that's the one they focus on.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这就是他们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: Their motivation, at least in my view, is absolutely no different than the adult to tell some kind of a scatological joke or whatever.
sentences.zh: 至少在我看来，他们的动机与成年人讲某种屎尿屁笑话之类的动机完全没有区别。

sentences.en: It's just that that's the material they have to act on about being funny and being shocking.
sentences.zh: 只不过那是他们手头仅有的、用来表现搞笑和追求震惊效果的素材。

sentences.en: Scatological.
sentences.zh: 排泄物的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I'm going to use that word in my book.
sentences.zh: 我要把这个词用在我的书里。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 对，我不知道。

sentences.en: Potty humor.
sentences.zh: 厕所幽默。

sentences.en: They get reinforced, right?
sentences.zh: 他们得到了正向反馈，对吧？

sentences.en: Whether it's good or bad.
sentences.zh: 无论是好的还是坏的。

sentences.en: But if, you know, the child says something, they're going to get laughs.
sentences.zh: 但如果孩子说了些什么，他们就会引来笑声。

sentences.en: You know, it could be uncomfortable laughs or it could be actual laughs or it could be scolding.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能是尴尬的笑声，也可能是真正的笑声，或者是遭到责骂。

sentences.en: But they get feedback and they know it will consistently get feedback.
sentences.zh: 但他们得到了反馈，并且知道这一定会持续获得反馈。

sentences.en: And so we've had a very hard time getting our five-year-old to stop saying poop all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们费了很大劲才让我们五岁的孩子停下总是说“便便”的嘴。

sentences.en: And it's just like ignoring it eventually is the...
sentences.zh: 最终选择忽视它大概是……

sentences.en: Well, and I've done, you know, developmental study of children's humor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我做过儿童幽默的发展研究。

sentences.en: And you see that's a particular stage.
sentences.zh: 你会发现那是一个特定的阶段。

sentences.en: And later they're going to do other shocking things or tell you a joke that wouldn't be appropriate either.
sentences.zh: 稍后他们会做其他令人震惊的事情，或者讲一些同样不太合适的笑话。

sentences.en: But it's just that with humor, a lot of humor is designed to have some sort of shocking quality to it because that's what makes it funny.
sentences.zh: 但这就是幽默的特点，很多幽默的设计都带有一种某种程度的震惊品质，因为这正是它好笑的地方。

sentences.en: So you use whatever is available at your own experience level.
sentences.zh: 所以你会利用你自身经验水平下所有能用得上的东西。

sentences.en: And there's been some interesting study of, you know, the differences in men's and women's humor.
sentences.zh: 而且有一些关于男女幽默差异的有趣研究。

sentences.en: And if you look at it closely, it has a lot to do with what have been their life experiences.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察，它很大程度上与他们的人生经历有关。

sentences.en: So it's just the same kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是完全一样的事情。

sentences.en: Potty humor is very funny to young children because that's a very important thing in their life.
sentences.zh: 厕所幽默对小孩子来说非常搞笑，因为那是他们生活中的一件大事。

sentences.en: If you recall, there's a lot of attention their adults have paid to how they manage that.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下，成年人对他们如何处理这件事投入了大量的关注。

sentences.en: So it's a good thing to make jokes about and to find funny.
sentences.zh: 所以拿它来开玩笑并觉得它好笑是一件很自然的事。

sentences.en: So shifting gears here, a few years ago, there were a number of news stories about major retailers such as Target getting rid of boys' and girls' labels in their toy departments.
sentences.zh: 我们换个话题，几年前，有许多新闻报道称，诸如塔吉特之类的大型零售商在其玩具专柜中取消了男孩和女孩的标签。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering what role gender plays in kids' toy preferences and in how they play with toys.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇性别在儿童对玩具的偏好以及他们玩玩具的方式中扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's all fabricated to some degree by marketing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这在某种程度上完全是营销制造出来的。

sentences.en: And when I was little, I just wanted to play with the Easy Bake Oven.
sentences.zh: 我小时候只想要一个培乐多烤箱。

sentences.en: But I think it was only in pink or something.
sentences.zh: 但我想它好像只有粉红色的还是怎么的。

sentences.en: And that's all I wanted, right?
sentences.zh: 而那正是我想要的，对吧？

sentences.en: And then it was like, no, that's a girl toy because it's, you know, it's pink and it's cooking.
sentences.zh: 然后大家就会说：不，那是女孩的玩具，因为它是粉红色的，而且是用来做饭的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I thought that was weird.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Now it's not.
sentences.zh: 现在不一样了。

sentences.en: You know, it's in different colors.
sentences.zh: 你看，它有不同的颜色了。

sentences.en: And for us, you know, we just, we get our kids whatever they want to play with.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，我们给孩子买任何他们想玩的玩具。

sentences.en: And we're trying not to say that's a gendered thing.
sentences.zh: 我们尽量不给它贴上性别的标签。

sentences.en: Sorry, our son has, you know, this probably more clothes that are labeled as girls' clothes in prior times.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我们的儿子拥有的被标为以前的女孩服装的衣服可能更多。

sentences.en: He has a lot of dresses and skirts.
sentences.zh: 他有很多连衣裙和半身裙。

sentences.en: And I think with like art, what is the art class?
sentences.zh: 我觉得就像艺术类服装，那个艺术品牌叫什么来着？

sentences.en: I think that's the brand.
sentences.zh: 我想那是这个牌子。

sentences.en: It's just a lot of, it's all mixed up together.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多款式，全都是混搭在一起的。

sentences.en: And there's no calling out, this is for a boy or a girl.
sentences.zh: 没有任何标签标明这是给男孩还是女孩的。

sentences.en: And I think a lot more parents feel that way now than they used to.
sentences.zh: 我想现在有更多父母有这种感觉了。

sentences.en: But the toy companies and the toy stores and all of them are still egregious about that because they are always determined to label boys' toys and girls' toys.
sentences.zh: 但玩具公司、玩具店以及所有这些机构在这方面依然十分过分，因为他们总是执着于给男孩玩具和女孩玩具贴标签。

sentences.en: I would agree with Barry that the typical child will play with anything that they find interesting.
sentences.zh: 我同意巴里的看法，典型的孩子会玩任何他们觉得有趣的玩具。

sentences.en: And there are times when dressing up is great for everybody.
sentences.zh: 有时候，玩变装对所有人来说都很棒。

sentences.en: And there's times when pushing cars around are great for everybody to be doing.
sentences.zh: 有时候，推着小汽车玩对所有人来说也都很棒。

sentences.en: And so children would not be making those boy and girl distinctions if adults were not promoting that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果不是成年人在推波助澜，孩子们根本不会做出这种男孩和女孩的区分。

sentences.en: And if you ask a lot of parents, unfortunately, even today, they would say, oh, I would only want to buy that for a boy or I'd only want to buy that for a girl.
sentences.zh: 如果你去问很多父母，不幸的是，即使在今天，他们也会说：哦，我只想给男孩买那个，或者我只想给女孩买那个。

sentences.en: But it's kind of working against that tide of advertisements and store directions to allow your child to have as wide a range of toys as they want to have, as Barry's trying to do.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是在逆着广告和商场指引的潮流而行，允许你的孩子拥有他们想拥有的尽可能广泛的玩具，就像巴里正在尝试做的那样。

sentences.en: And I do think it's worse now than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实觉得现在的情况比过去更糟糕了。

sentences.en: There was a one-time period in my professional career where there was a real attempt to take those labels off of the toys.
sentences.zh: 在我职业生涯的某个时期，曾有过一次真正的尝试，想要撕掉玩具上的那些标签。

sentences.en: And then it gradually crept back on everything again.
sentences.zh: 然后这些标签又逐渐回到了所有东西上。

sentences.en: So I'm hoping, if that's the case, that they're beginning to get rid of those labels again.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望，如果是这种情况的话，他们能再次开始撕掉这些标签。

sentences.en: It would be great.
sentences.zh: 那将是一件非常棒的事。

sentences.en: But I haven't seen much evidence of that as yet.
sentences.zh: 但我目前还没有看到太多这方面的迹象。

sentences.en: That sounds like it probably mirrors what's happening politically in a given country or in the world.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能反映了一个特定国家或世界上的政治现状。

sentences.en: So I'm sure that you both know adults who continue to be fascinated with toys.
sentences.zh: 所以我确信你们两个都认识那些对玩具持续着迷的成年人。

sentences.en: Do we ever really outgrow them?
sentences.zh: 我们真的会超越玩具、不再需要它们吗？

sentences.en: Do our toys just get bigger and more complicated and maybe more expensive?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们的玩具只是变得更大、更复杂、也许更贵了？

sentences.en: I think you never outgrow it, but the labels change.
sentences.zh: 我认为你永远不会对它失去兴趣，只是标签变了。

sentences.en: So instead of it being, I'm playing with this, it's something else.
sentences.zh: 所以不再是我在玩这个，而是变成了别的东西。

sentences.en: I have a hobby that I collect dolls or I have a hobby that I fly automatic planes or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我有一个收藏玩偶的爱好，或者我有一个遥控飞机等爱好的说法。

sentences.en: So play is a basic human characteristic.
sentences.zh: 所以游戏是人类的基本特征。

sentences.en: It is going to be present, hopefully, for all of us all our life.
sentences.zh: 希望在我们一生的岁月中，它都会伴随着我们。

sentences.en: And we should have times when we're playful and we're enjoying things that aren't getting graded or don't have to be paid for or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们应该有这样的时间：我们可以尽情玩耍，享受那些不用打分、不用花钱或者诸如此类的乐趣。

sentences.en: But I think that we call them by different names.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们给它们起了不同的名字。

sentences.en: As an adult, you're in a play, maybe, but you're not playing.
sentences.zh: 作为成年人，你可能身处一出戏中，但你并不是在玩。

sentences.en: But you're still pretending, you're taking a role, you're acting, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 但你仍然在假装，你在扮演一个角色，你在表演，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So that's a playful type of activity adults would do.
sentences.zh: 所以那是成年人会做的一种游戏性质的活动。

sentences.en: And that's true for a lot of other adult activities.
sentences.zh: 许多其他成年人的活动也是如此。

sentences.en: But we don't call them play.
sentences.zh: 但我们不称它们为游戏。

sentences.en: We call them hobbies or we call them a whole wide range of things.
sentences.zh: 我们称它们为爱好，或者我们称它们为形形色色的各种事情。

sentences.en: So I don't know why the word play doesn't continue to get used as much as it should be, because the playful quality of humans is one of our, in my view, best qualities.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道为什么“游戏”这个词没有像它应有的那样被广泛使用，因为在我看来，人类的游戏天性是我们最好的品质之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, in some areas, it stays.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些领域，它保留了下来。

sentences.en: Like when we're playing video games still as adults or playing sports, for example.
sentences.zh: 就像我们成年后仍然在玩电子游戏或进行体育运动一样。

sentences.en: But in general, it's not like, hey, guys, you want to come over to my house and play, right?
sentences.zh: 但在一般情况下，感觉不会是，嘿，伙计们，你们想来我家玩吗，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't call your friends as an adult and say that, unless you're saying cards, maybe.
sentences.zh: 成年后你不会给朋友打电话这么说，除非你可能是指打牌。

sentences.en: But yeah, the activities just get more challenging or they get more fine motor skills.
sentences.zh: 但是是的，这些活动只是变得更具挑战性，或者需要更多的精细运动技能。

sentences.en: So it goes from, you just think about puzzles, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它从，你只需要想想拼图，对吧？

sentences.en: You're starting with the four-piece puzzle as a little baby or toddler, and you get to like the hundred-piece puzzle.
sentences.zh: 你从作为小宝宝或幼儿时的四块拼图开始，然后你玩到像一百块的拼图。

sentences.en: And then an adult, you're still doing puzzles, but they're a thousand-piece, right?
sentences.zh: 然后作为一个成年人，你仍然在玩拼图，但它们是一千块的，对吧？

sentences.en: And maybe they have like...
sentences.zh: 也许它们有类似...

sentences.en: And it's still fun.
sentences.zh: 而且它依然很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's still fun, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它依然很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Or even skill-like based, you know?
sentences.zh: 或者甚至基于技能，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It goes from like stacking, you know, or the Nerf blasters to archery or something, right?
sentences.zh: 它从堆叠，你知道，或者从 Nerf 软弹枪到射击或类似的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like your motor skills get better, your budget gets higher, you can put more time and
sentences.zh: 就像你的运动技能变得更好，你的预算更高，你可以投入更多的时间和

sentences.en: money into these hobbies or recreation, and we just start to not associate it with that word because that word tends to mean for kids or trivial, right?
sentences.zh: 金钱到这些爱好或消遣中，我们只是开始不再将它与那个词联系起来，因为那个词往往意味着给小孩子玩的或微不足道的，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's still play.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然是游戏。

sentences.en: It's just, it's more fine-tuned, it's more advanced.
sentences.zh: 只是，它更精细，它更高级。

sentences.en: Yeah, and we call it a hobby, or we might just say, I want to do creative things instead of saying play, I'm creating, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们称之为爱好，或者我们可能只会说，我想做有创意的事情，而不是说玩，我在创造，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I think that my one concern, I guess I'll have to say, going back to that earlier when
sentences.zh: 我认为我的一点担忧，我想我得说，回到刚才我们谈论

sentences.en: we were talking about technology and how toys have now become so much more technologically designed.
sentences.zh: 科技以及玩具现在如何在技术上变得更加复杂的时候。

sentences.en: My view is the people who are having the playfulness are the people who are designing the stuff more than if it's a toy that you can only do one or two things with.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，相比于只能进行一两项活动的玩具，那些设计这些东西的人才真正拥有这种游戏精神。

sentences.en: And so I would hope that as the toys get more sophisticated, that they continue to have many different ways they can be used, because if a toy only has a few ways it can be used,
sentences.zh: 所以我希望随着玩具变得越来越复杂，它们能继续拥有多种不同的使用方式，因为如果一个玩具只有少数几种使用方式，

sentences.en: it either is not going to be played with very much, or it's going to make children no longer having opportunities to play.
sentences.zh: 要么它不会被玩太多，要么它会剥夺孩子们玩耍的机会。

sentences.en: If you're doing video games all the time, or you're doing things that are very structured, you are not getting a chance to have wonderful ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直都在玩电子游戏，或者你做的都是非常结构化的事情，你就不会有机会产生奇妙的想法。

sentences.en: There's been some really interesting research on adults who won MacArthur Awards, and when
sentences.zh: 有一些非常有趣的研究是关于获得麦克阿瑟奖的成年人的，当

sentences.en: they talked with a lot of them, they almost all said that what they most enjoyed when they
sentences.zh: 研究人员与他们中的许多人交流时，他们几乎都说他们小时候最喜欢的是

sentences.en: were younger, was what was called Small World Play, which is a kind of play that's allowed for elementary and older age kids.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“微观世界游戏”（Small World Play），这是一种适合小学生及更大年龄孩子的游戏。

sentences.en: And it's like designing little structures where you make little towns, or you make some kind of a small world.
sentences.zh: 就像设计小结构，在其中建造小城镇，或者创造某种微观世界。

sentences.en: And then you still continue to interact in that small world.
sentences.zh: 然后你继续在这个微观世界中互动。

sentences.en: But it's appropriate for an older child as compared to yourself taking on a pretend role or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但这比你自己扮演假想角色之类的更适合大一点的孩子。

sentences.en: So the kind of play that older kids, I hope, still have is where they can actually create the worlds and do things themselves, and not just rely on the technology that lets them
sentences.zh: 所以我希望大一点的孩子仍然能进行的这种游戏是，他们可以真正自己创造世界并做事情，而不只是依赖于让他们

sentences.en: go into somebody else's wonderful idea of what is play, where they don't really get to do their own ideas of play.
sentences.zh: 进入别人对游戏的奇妙构想的科技，在那里他们无法真正实现自己对游戏的构想。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're also advocating for basically more unstructured time, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来你也是在提倡基本上更多的非结构化时间，对吧？

sentences.en: For kids not to always be told, now you've got to go play tennis, because they may like tennis,
sentences.zh: 不要总是告诉孩子们，现在你们必须去打网球，因为他们可能喜欢网球，

sentences.en: but you're being forced to do it now, as opposed to, mom, I think I'm going to go out in the street now and play ball with the kids.
sentences.zh: 但你现在是被迫去打的，而不是像，妈妈，我想我现在要到街上去和孩子们一起玩球。

sentences.en: And Barry's done a lot about creativity.
sentences.zh: 巴里在创造力方面做了很多研究。

sentences.en: So you might want to talk a little bit about creativity's requirement for playfulness.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能想多聊聊创造力对游戏精神的需求。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a number of studies that have shown you're more creative when you're playing, or when you view an activity as play.
sentences.zh: 是的，有许多研究表明，当你在玩耍时，或者当你把一项活动看作是游戏时，你会更有创造力。

sentences.en: And I think to just build off of the small world comment, or the type of play, in today's
sentences.zh: 我想顺着关于微观世界的评论，或者那种游戏类型继续说，在当今

sentences.en: world, a lot of adults and kids are building those imaginary worlds, but it's in the computer.
sentences.zh: 世界，许多成年人和孩子都在构建那些想象中的世界，但它是在电脑里。

sentences.en: And it's in Minecraft and Fortnite.
sentences.zh: 它是在《我的世界》和《堡垒之夜》中。

sentences.en: And it is creative, you're building things, you're making up your own stuff, but it's also on a screen.
sentences.zh: 它确实具有创造性，你在建造东西，你在创造你自己的东西，但它也是在屏幕上。

sentences.en: So I don't know, there's pros and cons there, for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，这其中肯定有利也有弊。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there's something tactile.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，有一种触觉体验。

sentences.en: If you, for example, make dollhouses, or you've got a train set, and you've created a whole
sentences.zh: 如果你，例如，制作娃娃屋，或者你有一套火车模型，并且你创造了整个

sentences.en: layout of towns and so forth, it's very different from the experience of doing it just on a screen.
sentences.zh: 城镇布局等等，这与单纯在屏幕上操作的体验是非常不同的。

sentences.en: So as we're moving into the holiday season, I think I opened with this and people are out buying
sentences.zh: 随着我们进入假期，我想我是以此开场的，人们都在外出购买

sentences.en: toys, do you have any guidance, suggestions for parents who are looking for gifts for their
sentences.zh: 玩具，你对那些正在为孩子寻找礼物的父母有什么指导、建议吗，无论是经典款还是其他什么，我的意思是，我不是要求你

sentences.en: kids' toys that, whether they're classics or there's something, I mean, I'm not asking you to
sentences.zh: 推荐某个特定的品牌或产品，而是关于父母在试图给孩子买节日礼物时应该寻找什么的这种概念？

sentences.en: endorse a particular brand or a product, but sort of the concept of what would you recommend parents be looking for as they're trying to get their kids' holiday presents?
sentences.zh: 哇，好的，我经常遇到这个问题，然后我就卡壳了。

sentences.en: Wow, okay, I get this a lot, and then I freeze.
sentences.zh: 从棋盘游戏来看，结合我对创造力的研究，我有很多认为能培养创造力的最爱。

sentences.en: Board game-wise, going to my research on creativity, I have a lot of favorites that I think build creative skills.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的游戏其实叫《行动代号》（Codenames），这是一个关于发散性思维和

sentences.en: My favorite game is actually called Codenames, and it's a game about divergent thinking and
sentences.zh: 收敛性思维的游戏，它是一个文字游戏，但现在已经衍生出了不同的主题版本。

sentences.en: convergent thinking, and it's a word game, but it's now branched out into different properties.
sentences.zh: 所以有迪士尼版、漫威版和哈利波特版，因此你很可能会找到一个能与你的孩子产生共鸣的版本。

sentences.en: So there's a Disney version and a Marvel version and a Harry Potter version, and so you're likely to find one that resonates with your child.
sentences.zh: 但就它培养的创造力技能而言，我真的很喜欢那款游戏。

sentences.en: But I really do like that game as far as the creative skills that it builds.
sentences.zh: 我也偏爱任何与烹饪和食物相关的东西，而且我不认为它一定需要是某个事物的玩具版本。

sentences.en: I'm also partial to anything related to cooking and food, and I don't necessarily think it needs to be a toy version of a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是一定要推荐那种容易烤箱（Easy-Bake Oven）。

sentences.en: So I'm not necessarily advocating for the easy-bake oven.
sentences.zh: 我推荐的可能是真正的儿童刀具套装，虽然是更安全的刀具，但它们仍然是刀，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm advocating for maybe the kid's knife set that are actually knives, and it's the safer knives, but they're still knives, right?
sentences.zh: 还有像儿童削皮器、蔬菜削皮器这样的东西。

sentences.en: And like the kid peeler, vegetable peeler.
sentences.zh: 如果还有其他好玩的、孩子们可以和你在厨房一起玩的产品，例如，像压面机，对吧？

sentences.en: And if there's any other fun products that children can play with you in the kitchen, for example, like a pasta maker, right?
sentences.zh: 那个手摇压面机，至少一个月一次，孩子们把它当作玩具，我们在里面一起做饭。

sentences.en: The hand-cranked pasta maker, at least once a month, the children view that as a toy, and we're making food together.
sentences.zh: 而且那并不是一个很贵的厨房工具。

sentences.en: And it's not that expensive of a kitchen tool.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我的建议是跳出玩具货架去思考。

sentences.en: So just, I guess, think beyond the toy aisle is my recommendation.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 我的建议是确保有一些全家人都能玩的游戏。

sentences.en: My suggestion would be sure to have some games that everyone in the family can play.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想你的童年，你会记起一些最美好的时光，那是全家人聚在一起玩某种游戏的时候。

sentences.en: If you think back to your childhood, you can remember some of the best times when your whole family gathered together and played some kind of game.
sentences.zh: 它可能不是一个非常高智商的游戏，但它是你们可以一起做的事情。

sentences.en: It might not have been a very intellectual game, but it was something that you could do together.
sentences.zh: 你学到的事情之一就是，如果赢的不是你，如何表现得更有体育精神。

sentences.en: And one of the things you learn is how to be a little better sport if you're not always the one who's coming out winning the game.
sentences.zh: 但我认为与家人一起参与游戏的这种想法非常重要。

sentences.en: But I think that that idea of engaging with your family and play is a very important one.
sentences.zh: 我的另一个建议是，从游戏价值来看，你提供的开放式玩具越多越好。

sentences.en: The other suggestion I would have is that the more open-ended toys you can provide, the better in terms of play value.
sentences.zh: 可以以多种不同方式使用的东西。

sentences.en: Things that can be used in a number of different ways.
sentences.zh: 也许它们一开始是某种样子，但随后你可以把它们变成其他东西。

sentences.en: Maybe they start out a certain way, but then you can kind of transform them into other things.
sentences.zh: 还有，它们不一定是那种最受欢迎的知名玩具品牌之类的内容。

sentences.en: And also, the idea that they don't have to be the most popular kind of name toy, toy brand, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而是非常简单的东西。

sentences.en: But very simple things.
sentences.zh: 例如，球仍然是非常受欢迎的玩具。

sentences.en: Balls, for example, are still extremely popular toys.
sentences.zh: 只需准备几种不同大小的球并和它们一起玩。

sentences.en: And just having a few different sizes of balls and playing with them.
sentences.zh: 但你确实需要有其他孩子或者家庭成员来一起玩。

sentences.en: But you do need to have either other children to play with or family members to do it.
sentences.zh: 在我早期的很多研究中，我发现孩子们过去常常和许多其他孩子在户外玩耍。

sentences.en: And in a lot of my early research, I found kids used to play outside with a lot of other kids.
sentences.zh: 而现在这似乎不那么常见了。

sentences.en: And that seems to have been less common now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们没有在户外和其他孩子一起玩，那么家人就需要和他们一起玩，或者他们必须在学校有更多机会与其他孩子玩耍，

sentences.en: And so, if they're not playing with other kids outside, then the family needs to play with them, or they have to play more
sentences.zh: 或在某个他们可以学习如何互谅互让的地方。

sentences.en: with other kids at school, or somewhere where they can learn some of the give and take.
sentences.zh: 正如皮亚杰所说，促进他们的道德发展。

sentences.en: And as Piaget would say, enhance their moral development.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢两广。

sentences.en: Well, thank you both.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们为正在寻找玩具的父母以及其他儿童照看者提供了一些好的建议和指导，特别是在一年中的这个时候。

sentences.en: And I hope that we provided some good advice and guidance to parents and other caregivers of children who are looking for toys, particularly around this time of year.
sentences.zh: 但其实随时都可以，因为玩具是没有季节性的，对吧？

sentences.en: But all the time, because toys are, there's no season, right?
sentences.zh: 玩具是属于所有时间的。

sentences.en: Toys are for all time.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢二位。

sentences.en: So thank you both.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
